steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper; draw a 9-inch circle on the parchment paper.

Beat egg whites in a glass, metal, or ceramic bowl until stiff but not dry. Gradually add sugar, about 1 tablespoon at a time, beating well after each addition. Continue beating until meringue is thick, white, and glossy.
Gently fold in cornstarch, vanilla extract, and lemon juice.

Spoon mixture inside the circle drawn on the parchment paper. Working from the center, spread mixture toward the outside edge and build the edge slightly. This should leave a slight depression in the center.
Bake in the preheated oven until meringue is dry and sounds hollow when tapped, about 1 hour. Cool on a wire rack.
Beat heavy cream in a medium bowl until stiff peaks form; set aside. Remove meringue from the parchment paper and place on a flat serving plate.
Fill center of meringue with whipped cream and top with kiwi slices.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Pavlova
raw_recipe.description: This pavlova has a crisp meringue exterior and soft, fluffy center; top with mounds of whipped cream and fresh fruit for a showstopping dessert.

video.description: In this video, we show you how to make a light dessert of sweetened meringue topped with whipped cream and fresh fruit. We'll also share a trick on getting the most volume out of the egg whites.

review.reviewBody: FANTASTIC. Growing up in Australia this dish was part of our national identity, but here in the US I could just never get it right. This recipe is just as it should be. We always let this dish cool in the oven - just turn the oven off at the end of the cooking time and leave it there (even overnight!). For those who have found that it sometimes sticks, in Australia we would coat the paper with a thin dusting of corn starch before spooning the mix onto the baking tray.

I make this recipe all the time! Super easy. Make sure that the eggs are room temperature before you begin otherwise it will take forever to stiffen, Also make sure your bowl is super clean and use either glass or metal (no plastic because they retain grease). I like to add about 6 tables spoons of powdered sugar and a tsp of vanilla to the heavy cream… Sometimes i make mini pavlovas just decrease the time to 30 minutes and you can get about 36 mini pavlovas about the size of an egg yolk.

Turned out well. I couldn't get a round shape, so it was more oblong. I beat in the vanilla and cornstarch at the end rather than folding. Topped with vanilla whipped cream, sliced mango and passionfruit.

I followed others' suggestion about cutting down the sugar to only 1 cup and I'm glad I did. The pavlova came out awesome and many calories were saved! It is definitely very sweet and not something you can just nibble on...you NEED the whipped cream and tangy fruits to balance it out!! I went the extra step of looking for passionfruit puree (found it in frozen form at a Latin supermarket) and turned it into a syrup as it was too sour if left alone. I prepped one slice with and one without the passionfruit syrup and omgosh it made all the difference! So if you can, I'd highly recommend finding the passionfruit puree for your pavlova. To make the syrup, I bought 2 frozen packages of puree and added 3/4c sugar and gently boiled the whole thing down to 1/2 the volume. One tip I read and used is to use caster sugar because it has smaller granules and can melt into the egg whites faster? Another tip I read is to bake at low temp to prevent cracking. I decided to bake at 275F for 50 minutes and 200F for 15 minutes. After that I just turned off the oven and left the door closed for another hour to cool down gradually. Mine came out picture perfect with minimal cracking. Loved it and will make it again!

I followed the recipe exactly as written. You absolutely must follow the instructions of mixing in 1 tablespoon of sugar at a time into the egg whites. I rushed it with the first batch and ended up tossing it. The second time I did as instructed and it took 5-6 minutes to mix all of the sugar in. It came out so good!!! I would probably reduce sugar to 1 cup as it im awake a bit sweet but I tend to not add much sugar to my fresh whipped cream so that evens it out. I read that you could store it in a cool oven with the door closed (without toppings) as storing in the fridge could cause condensation. It worked for me! I just added whipped cream and fruit 2 hours before serving.

I’ve been making pavlova for years and trying do fervent recipes. This was the BEST pavlova I’ve made. I divided into eight individual pavlovas about 4” in diameter each. I then created a “make your own pavlova” experience for my guests. We had the whipped cream, berries, and I had some shaved chocolate as option. Very fun and rave reviews on taste. I also reduced sugar to 1 cup, and turned oven off after one hour, opened the oven door for few minutes, then shut the door and kept pavlovas in oven until completely cool. PERFECT

Bake at 250 F. I used 6 egg whites and 1/2 cup baking Splenda. Combine cornstarch, lemon juice & vanilla before adding to egg whites. Everything else the same except after one hour, turned off oven and left in oven until the oven was completely cool. (Do not open oven while it is cooking and cooling.). It was delish. I had never had this dessert until I lived in New Zealand where it is a favorite dessert. So good and really easy to make.

Made it for my Australian husband today and it turned out PERFECTLY. I did it exactly as is, but always find it to be grossly sweet. Does this recipe still turn out with half the sugar? This is it cooling. Have yet to add fruit and cream

I have been wanting to make pavlova for a long time.The first round I made pretty much per directions. It cracked, was a light golden color and was not pretty at all. So I did a little reading and then tried again. First, I reduce the oven temp to 250. Combine sugar and cornstarch and slowly added to the whipped egg whites. I used vinegar instead of lemon juice also. When baking your pavlova when it is done just leave it in the oven to cool for a few hours or even overnight. It turned out perfectly that way and everyone in my family loved it.

I made it twice with the ingredients as is. I didn't find it too sweet as I am pretty sure that's how a meringue is supposed to taste. I topped with lightly sweetened whipped cream and unsweetened strawberries which balanced nicely. I took the reviewer's advice to mix the vanilla/lemon/cornstarch together before adding - key. It was fantastic both times - the only changes i made the second time were that I used the mixer to add the vanilla combo (instead of folding) and I used an 8" circle to measure so that it would pile up higher - definitely improvements. Thank for this recipe - no need to find another. So delicious and so impressive!

This is my go-to recipe for pavlova. When it's done baking, turn off the heat and let it cool down in the oven (I use a wooden spoon to keep the oven slightly open). Another great tip would be to add the whipped cream and sliced fruits right before serving; the pavlova stays crisp that way. I like adding fresh vanilla beans into it. Those little black specks make it look great!

Followed another reader's suggestion to mix cornstarch in the sugar and another reader's suggestion to use two cups of sugar instead of two and a quarter. I added one and a half tsp if vanilla instead of one. Turned out beautifully!

This recipe was really quite simple - and it turned out delicious. I made my own whipped cream recipe and put berries on it as that is what is in season now. Everyone loved it and my daughter said "10/10 - would eat again"!
I love this version for the base. It always turns out well. I do go a little off script for the toppings, but this is a very reliable base.
Delicious, tasty, and beautiful presentation with strawberries

Tripled the recipe because my family loves pavlova. I used vinegar instead of lemon juice. It turned out fantastic! I serve with a variety of fresh fruit and berries alongside the pavlova. I also serve the whipped cream on the side as I don't care for it. This way, everyone can build their own dessert according to personal preference. Lemon curd is another great side to go with pavlova.
Light, refreshing, & DELICIOUS. A little time consuming but SO worth it.Even more delectable with a cup of coffee! 😍

Turned out great, one of my better attempts but I think it could use less sugar. My family in Ireland make this, the approach is a little different but theirs is less sweet. I think next time I would do only a cup of sugar not 1 1/2
OMG this was so easy to make and the instructions were easy to follow, LOVE IT
Will be making this again! So light and refreshing! Great for a naturally gluten free dessert!
